sentences.text: A systematic review of twelve studies, most employing convolutional neural network architectures, evaluated whether artificial intelligence can generate synthetic post-contrast brain MRI images from low-dose inputs to reduce gadolinium contrast agent usage.
Across these investigations involving 3846 patients, the AI-generated images yielded a pooled peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.91 dB and a structural similarity index of 91.81%.
However, significant variation between the included studies meant that these combined statistical results were interpreted only as descriptive figures rather than definitive averages.

Qualitative assessments indicated that the synthetic images were generally considered diagnostically acceptable or similar to full-dose images, although subtle differences in how lesions and artifacts appeared were noted.
The authors conclude that high variation between studies, limited external validation, and a lack of clinically focused diagnostic outcomes restrict the generalizability of the current evidence.
